expert_role: Graphic designer specialising in competition boards; gatekeeper auditing cited sources and VTC rules (round 4, packet P13)

findings.issue: The spec still rests on a brief nobody has checked. P13-S01 is still opened:false and the register due 23-24 Oct is empty today (21 Oct). Every rule from the brief therefore remains a transcription from the project description: exact 4 boards, landscape, the 40/30/20/10 weights, the 20 items, the skyline viewpoint, any file-naming rule and the site placement. I re-read the competition page: it has no board specs, and Terms 4.5 and 4.8 defer to the brief. An entrant who relies on HR-03, HR-04 or R-01 now is relying on unverified data.
findings.fix: Treat the populated register as a release condition for any entrant-facing build, not a schedule item. Store the English PDF with its SHA-256, filename and language version. Two members transcribe every rule with a page number. Also transcribe the skyline-viewpoint definition, any file-naming or UIC rule, the portal form fields and the site plan's placement and rotation. Flip evidence_status only after both checks.

findings.issue: The eligibility gate covers only half the risk. Terms 3.3.5 disqualify an 'employee, intern, contractor, officer, or director of the Organizer', yet the Terms never name the Organizer (2.1 is generic; 1.2 names only the brand BUILDNER SL). The competition page says 'Organized by Buildner, in collaboration with the City of Vancouver and ... UBC SALA'. A SALA student who is a UBC employee (TA, RA or GAA), or a member employed by the City, may be directly ineligible, with no 'associate' question involved. C8 and the attestation do not ask this. The timeline also says to start identity verification on Fri 23 Oct 'once C8 is sent', before any answer arrives. That contradicts the spec's own rule that G-00 comes first, because verification fees are non-refundable once started (7.4.1) and registration fees are not repayable (7.3).
findings.fix: Extend C8 to ask: 'Does Organizer in 3.3 include the City of Vancouver or UBC/SALA, and are UBC student employees (TA/RA) or City employees eligible?' Add the attestation item 'no employment, internship or contract with UBC, the City of Vancouver or Buildner SL'. Record the Organizer identity in the register. Move identity verification to after C8 is answered, or after a logged, N-signed 'risk accepted' decision on 27 Oct.

findings.issue: Two planned actions may themselves break the communication rules. The spec plans to obtain cone ceilings 'confirmed by the City' and names views@vancouver.ca as the contact. The page says 'All communication regarding the competition should only be carried out with Buildner staff'. Terms 5.2 bar approaching the Commissioning Party, an undefined term that may cover the City as collaborator. The Shape Your City page also invites non-formal ideas to higherbuildings@vancouver.ca, which entrants might use and which could count as publication or approach.
findings.fix: Add a no-contact rule (for example G-00b): no contact with City staff, UBC SALA staff acting for the competition, or jurors about the competition. Route ceiling and viewpoint questions to Buildner as C11. Read only public City documents. Warn against sending entry material to higherbuildings@vancouver.ca while the entry is live.

findings.issue: G-00 can end in a deadlock. 'Risk accepted' shows amber 'never green', but G-05 allows the first upload only after 'all hard rules and gates (G-00..G-04) pass', and the method says 'unresolved G-00 sets blocking=true'. If Buildner never answers C8, the release gate never opens, even after the team decided on 27 Oct to accept the risk and pay. The spec does not say whether amber blocks.
findings.fix: Define gate states as pass, accepted-risk and fail. Accepted-risk unblocks M06c only with N signatures and the date of C8 sent. Fail always blocks. Write the rule into the registry and add a unit test.

findings.issue: The tool is open-source and public, and the team builds it and its demos for a UBC SALA course. G-04 checks only assets in the tool's own asset_visibility. Copies outside that store are not checked: repo fixtures, README screenshots, pilot renders in issues or pull requests, forked community modules carrying the team's massing, and course demo videos. Any of these would be previous publication under 4.1 and traceable identity under 5.1, for example through reverse image search. Default board templates or captions that carry the tool's name or styling would also tie a board to the SALA team for a SALA juror.
findings.fix: Extend G-04 to a repo and public-asset scan: hashes of board-linked assets checked against the git history, release assets and the community store. Pilots and fixtures use a dummy, non-entry tower. Add the tool name, repo URL and course code to the per-team deny-list. Exported templates and AI captions carry no tool branding; the caption should read only 'AI-assisted image'.

findings.issue: Size optimisation and export reach entrants only after the deadline. Composer M06b moves to v1 (10 Dec), so before 30 Nov entrants get a validator that can fail a board but cannot fix it. They will export from InDesign, Illustrator, Photoshop or Affinity, whose JPEG export embeds XMP fields (creator tool, document IDs, sometimes author names) and uses tool-specific chroma subsampling. The scope item 'export (PDF/JPG, size optimisation)' is not met for real entrants.
findings.fix: Add a core re-encode action to M06v (about 1 person-day, using jSquash already listed). It decodes the board, converts it to sRGB, sets baseline 4:4:4 explicitly, searches quality under 9.5 x 10^6 bytes, strips metadata and re-validates. Publish tested export recipes for the four desktop tools, each confirmed by a validator round-trip.

findings.issue: The document register omits documents the City links directly on its review page. The Shape Your City page, re-read 21 Oct (last updated 13 July 2026), links a Granville Street Plan, a Bay Parkade rezoning FAQ and the Vancouver Lookout exhibit boards. It says the competition 'seeks design ideas for taller buildings in specific downtown locations'. The brief's 'retail high street' and the placement-dependent Granville Street view 20 make these relevant to the policy reflection and to the site placement, but the register lists only the 1997 policy, the Public Views Guidelines and the OGL.
findings.fix: Add these three documents to the document_register with hash and retrieval date; their text was not readable by fetch, so a person must download them. Add them to M08 governing_policy_set and to the M03 placement check (does the brief's block match a real location?).

findings.issue: Several metrics break the spec's own rule that evidence_status is 'the weakest element its pass/fail rests on'. HR-06 anonymity (deny-list and seeds are team design), G-01 (manual attestation), G-03 (licence compatibility is a human judgement), G-05 ('the gate itself is tool design') and D-01 (7-day and 2-day buffers are team choices) are all marked verified. M02 'Plan cut height convention' has team-set bad bounds but is also marked verified. A typed node would treat team controls as sourced.
findings.fix: Split each record into clause_evidence and method_evidence, or set evidence_status to team_assumption wherever the threshold or method is team-made. Add a schema test that a metric whose basis says 'team' cannot carry evidence_status verified.

findings.issue: Registration closes '29 October 2026' with no hour (page re-read). D-02 counts days to a date, not to an instant. If the close is read as start of day London time (GMT after 25 Oct), it falls at 28 Oct 17:00 Vancouver, a day earlier than the banner implies.
findings.fix: Store a worst-case instant of 2026-10-29T00:00Z (28 Oct 17:00 Vancouver) and show it beside 23:59Z. Keep the 27 Oct registration target.

findings.issue: The competition page currently says 'only recognized university staff can apply for the reduced student rate', which taken literally excludes students. Fees are EUR 140 standard and EUR 120 student, plus 4.5% VAT, in euros (Terms 7.4); the spec records none of this. Student Award eligibility drives the M07 award track, and the first users are students.
findings.fix: Make C10 mandatory and send it with C8 by 23 Oct. Record the fees and currency in the register. Keep the Student Award track amber until answered.

findings.issue: The spec treats the 24 dataset polygons as 'all' protected views (re-verified: total_count 24). The 2024 Public Views Guidelines, still unread, are the governing source. The dataset may not cover every view or sub-view and has no heights, so 'all 24' may not mean all protected views.
findings.fix: Rename the set 'all 24 cones in the open dataset (modified 2026-10-19)' and add an UNVERIFIED flag on whether the dataset is complete against the Guidelines. A person reads the Guidelines PDF in a browser by 24 Oct.

findings.issue: The apparent-height illustration (atan of 300 m over 5 km, 3.4 degrees) ignores eye elevation; QE Park is about 125 m ASL against a downtown base near sea level. The tower-share metric uses top_y - base_y even when the base is hidden by terrain or towers. Focal-length suggestions will therefore be too short.
findings.fix: Use visible top minus visible base after ray-casting, and use eye elevation from the terrain. Take the skyline viewpoint definition from the brief register rather than only from the apex inference.

findings.issue: The ratio good band is +/-0.005 and the bad band is outside +/-0.02, leaving 0.005-0.02 undefined. Landscape also remains unverified until the register is checked.
findings.fix: State amber for 0.005-0.02 and show it as amber in both modules from the single HR-04 record.

verdict: Gate fails. Round 3 fixes landed: Q&A routing, all 24 cones, site_georeference, ZDR and the rule registry. But entrants still cannot rely on P13. The brief register is empty, so every board rule remains a project-description transcription. Eligibility is only half-covered: the Terms never name the Organizer, while the page lists the City and UBC SALA as collaborators, and verification fees would be spent before C8 is answered. The method plans City contact, against the Buildner-only rule. Accepted-risk G-00 can deadlock release. The public repo is outside the previous-publication gate. Before 30 Nov entrants get a validator that cannot repair a failing JPEG. Web search budget was exhausted, so checks used direct fetches only.
